1.deliverable: A one-to-two page application brief (brief.md) that someone else could build from without guessing.
setup: Create a folder for your project, for example taskboard-brief.
Inside it, create an empty file called brief.md (any text editor works).
Optional: clone the Taskboard example to compare your brief with a finished project.

code.title: Brief template (brief.md)
code.body:
# Application brief: <name>

## Users and problem
Who: 
Their difficulty: 
How they cope today: 

## One-sentence description

## Application type and trade-off

## Core user journey
1.

## User stories
As a <user>, I want <goal> so that <reason>.
Acceptance: Given … When … Then …

## Quality, constraints, assumptions

## Open questions

code.title: Ask AI to review, not build
code.body:
Here is my application brief. Do not write any code.
List every question a developer would need answered
before starting, and point out contradictions or
vague requirements. Number your findings.

2.deliverable: A diagram of your application's parts plus a written trace of one user action from click to database and back.
setup: Open the Taskboard example (or your own app) in your editor.
Install Node.js LTS if you want to run it locally.
Have a blank page or a diagram tool ready (paper is fine).

code.title: Run the example locally
code.body:
cd taskboard
npm install
npm run dev
# open the printed http://localhost address

code.title: Watch one request
code.body:
1. Open the browser's Developer Tools → Network tab.
2. Create a task in the app.
3. Click the new request. Note: method, URL, status code,
   request body and response body.

code.title: Trace template
code.body:
## Action: create a task
1. Interface: user types a title and presses Save
2. Request: POST /api/tasks  {"title": "…"}
3. Backend: checks the user is signed in, validates title
4. Database: INSERT INTO tasks (title, owner_id) …
5. Response: 201 Created + the new task
6. Interface: list updates
What could fail at each step?

3.deliverable: A running copy of the project, a short map of its folders, and one small change committed on its own branch.
setup: Create a free GitHub account if you don't have one.

code.title: Reproduce the project
code.body:
git clone https://github.com/solomonpromise/taskboard.git
cd taskboard
cp .env.example .env   # fill in values, never commit .env
npm install
npm test
npm run dev

code.title: Make a controlled change
code.body:
git checkout -b change-empty-state-text
# edit one file
git status
git diff
git add -A
git commit -m "Clarify empty task list message"
git log --oneline -3

code.title: Project map (PROJECT_MAP.md)
code.body:
| Folder / file | What it holds | Safe to change? |
|---|---|---|
| src/ | application code | yes, with tests |
| package.json | dependencies and scripts | carefully |
| .env | secrets | never commit |

4.deliverable: A compact design pack: system diagram, technology choices with reasons, data model, integrations and quality trade-offs.
setup: Have your Part 1 brief and Part 2 trace open.
Create a folder called design/ in your project.

code.title: Decision record (design/decisions.md)
code.body:
## Decision: <what was chosen>
Context: what problem forced a choice
Options considered: A, B, C
Choice: B
Why: 
Trade-offs accepted: 
Revisit when:

code.title: Data model sketch
Ask AI to challenge the design
code.body:
Here is my design pack. Act as a sceptical reviewer.
Where is it over-built for a first version? Where will
it break under 10x users? Which decision lacks a reason?

5.deliverable: A working first version built in small, reviewed steps, with tests passing and a log of what AI produced and what you checked.
setup: Pick an AI coding tool (an AI app builder or an editor assistant).
Start from your design pack and a clean Git branch.
Make sure npm test runs, even if there are no tests yet.

code.title: A well-prepared task prompt
code.body:
Goal: let a signed-in user mark a task as done.
Context: tasks table has a `done` boolean (see design/).
Scope: only the task list and its API route.
Do not: change auth, add libraries, touch other pages.
Done when: toggling persists after reload and a test
covers another user being unable to change my task.

code.title: Small test example
Review each change
code.body:
git diff            # read every line AI changed
npm test            # must pass
git commit -am "Toggle task done"

6.deliverable: A live deployment plus a maintenance guide covering monitoring, backups, recovery and how to make future changes safely.
setup: Choose a host (many AI builders include one-click publishing).
Store production secrets in the host's settings, not in code.
Have your first version passing its tests.

code.title: Pre-release check
code.body:
npm test
npm run build
git tag v1.0.0
git push --tags
